newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. Treasuries easier in directionless Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries easier in directionless Tokyo.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were easier, but the market lacked direction by Tokyo midday on Monday as operators refrained from taking fresh positions amid a dearth of fresh incentives, traders said.
"Light profit-taking capped prices, but underlying sentiment stayed bullish," a commercial bank trader said.
Traders said the firmness of the dollar against the yen after the Group of Seven summit had no direct impact on Treasury prices so far this morning.
The 6-5/8 percent 30-year bond stood at 99-15/32, yielding 6.67 percent, against 99-16/32 in New York on Friday.
The September T-bond futures contract stood at 112-15/32, down 2/32 from the previous close. It was moving in tight range of 112-14/32 to 112-16/32.
In New York, Treasury prices closed mostly higher as technical buying took the long end of the market to four-month highs before giving way to late session profit taking.

Traders expect the underlying bullish mood to continue due to strong bargain hunting interest and strong technical factors. "Fading speculation of a credit-tightening should continue to provide support," the trader said. "But strong buying factors are needed for prices to test higher levels."
